title: Dynamics 365 Business Central AL Development
description:
Business Central covers standard processes, but sooner or later a company needs an extra field, approval step or business rule. In this Knowledge Nugget Mirko Peters explains for beginners and functional consultants how AL and extensions customize Business Central safely without touching the base application.
In this episode
00:00 – Intro: one small change in Business Central00:40 – Why businesses customize Business Central03:35 – AL and extensions: the safe add-on model06:39 – The main AL building blocks11:04 – Events, triggers and business rules14:59 – Where AL development happens17:34 – Example: a customer rewards add-on18:55 – Your AL development starting point
Key takeaways
AL is Microsoft's language for Business Central, and extensions keep custom work separate from the base application so updates do not turn into major rebuilds.Tables, pages, table and page extensions, codeunits, triggers and event subscribers each have one job, and shared business rules belong in a codeunit.AL development happens in Visual Studio Code with the AL language extension, testing belongs in a sandbox, and Git keeps a history of every change.
Worth quoting
“Instead of rewriting the standard application, developers build a separate add-on that connects to it, keeping the standard part in place while the company's own changes sit beside it” – Mirko Peters (01:44)
“changing something just because it looks different from an old system creates extra work later, so good custom work starts with a clear business reason.” – Mirko Peters (02:48)
